newsitem.title: BELGIUM: No Alitalia ruling before March end - EU Commission.
newsitem.headline: No Alitalia ruling before March end - EU Commission.

text.p: Italian airline Alitalia will have to wait until March or early April for a European Commission ruling on the fate of its planned cash injection, a senior Commission official said on Thursday.

Philip Lowe, chief aide to European Transport Commissioner Neil Kinnock, said inquiries were coming to an end into the planned multi-trillion-lire aid package and restructuring plan for Italy's mainly state-owned carrier.
"They are nearing a completion...we would expect an earliest decision in March or early April," Lowe told a news conference.
Alitalia plans to supplement two payments of 1.5 trillion lire ($940 million) in 1996 and 1997 with an offer allowing employees to buy 313 billion lire of stock over the same period.

Lowe later told Reuters the Commission was also looking into pension-related subsidies worth a further 160 billion lire to the airline, bringing the grand total for planned aid to 3.473 trillion ($2.171 billion).
Lowe said the Italians had defended the pension-related funds as a general measure to all industry.
"If they are classified as state aid then the procedure is likely to lengthen," he added.
The Commission, which has powers to vet and alter state aid measures to EU airlines, announced its inquiry in October, rejecting Alitalia's initial case for a bail-out.

Possible changes the Commission has said it might require include additional asset sales to those already offered, a longer payment schedule, further reductions in operating costs, an active search for foreign partner airlines and an adjustment to expansion plans. ($=1,600 lire)
